A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSU research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original adaptation experiments across five languages and two model sizes, including benchmark results, freezing ablations, and supplementary baseline analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds coding, reduced-data, OLMo 3, translation-formatting, and computational-cost evaluations.

M1.justification: Source-based importance scoring, column-wise mask construction, and masked-gradient continual pre-training remain unchanged. Alternative scoring methods also already appear in v1; the additional evaluations introduce no new SSU component.

E1.justification: V2 adds HumanEval coding evaluation for both model sizes after each of the five existing language adaptations. Existing languages, training corpora, and natural-language benchmarks remain. The translation proxy reuses the existing MT setup.

E2.justification: The corresponding original comparisons retain their comparator membership. LoTA and S2FT were already evaluated in v1 Tables 6 and 14 and move to v2 Tables 14 and 15. Added experiments reuse previously evaluated methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 20M-token adaptation condition alongside the original 200M-token setting, evaluates Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, and introduces HumanEval pass@1. Appendix D.6 adds strict MT scoring requiring language consistency, matching sentence counts, and terminal punctuation. Original experimental settings and translated prompts are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test preservation of coding capabilities, robustness to reduced training data and OLMo 3, translation-formatting failures, and computational overhead. Existing freezing-structure, scoring-method, calibration-size, and baseline-sparsity analyses are retained, with several relocated to Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-run averages for the listed generative tasks and single deterministic classification evaluations in Section 4.5 and Appendix C. No new seed-reporting, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the original per-language and LoTA/S2FT tables retain identical numerical results. V2 adds results in Tables 4, 5, 16, and 17 and timing measurements in Appendix B.1. For example, the new OLMo 3 comparison reports 1.1% average source degradation for SSU versus 5.9% for FFT, with 17.3% target gains for SSU.

T1.justification: The importance-score formulas, column aggregation, and masked-update mathematics are unchanged. Appendix D.5 relocates the existing conceptual theoretical discussion; no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: adaptation using unlabeled target data, proactive preservation through source-guided column freezing, and target performance competitive with full fine-tuning. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets coding preservation as evidence for universal functional capabilities and reduced-data results as evidence of beneficial regularization. Appendix D.6 adds an explanation of target-language formatting failures. A new Limitations section explicitly discusses comparator scope, incomplete hyperparameter searches, and potentially nonoptimal configurations.

D1.justification: V2 adds scoring and training times, implementation rules for the translation proxy, and explicit model identifiers and license information in Appendices B.1, D.6, and F. Existing hyperparameters, software versions, hardware descriptions, and the code-access link remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting the new evaluations and discussions of replay and forgetting-aware pruning, including Sainz et al. (2025) and Huang et al. (2025). Selected earlier references and discussions are removed, including Alexandrov et al. (2024) and Elhady et al. (2025). The core source-focused positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially condenses and rewrites the main narrative, particularly related work and results. Existing analyses move into Appendix D.1–D.3 and D.5, while limitations, ethical considerations, licenses, and AI-use disclosures receive a reorganized section structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to double-column layout, with widespread table and caption reformatting. Figure 1 is redrawn and relocated; existing ablations are consolidated. The original multi-method freezing plot moves to Figure 3, an SSU-only display becomes Figure 2, and four new result tables are added.

improvement.justification: Coding, reduced-data, and OLMo 3 evaluations strengthen evidence about applicability while preserving the original empirical results. Timing measurements and explicit tuning limitations improve transparency. The gain is qualified by the translation proxy's limited validity: Appendix D.6 acknowledges that its formatting requirements are not explicitly requested in the prompts.
